plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single labeled diagram of a simple pendulum hanging from a beige horizontal bar. A dashed vertical drops from the attachment point to mark the equilibrium direction, and a solid line making an angle labeled theta with it runs down and to the right; the string is labeled L and a small gray sphere at its lower end is labeled m. A dashed arc labeled s connects the equilibrium line to the bob. A dark blue arrow along the string points from the bob back toward the pivot, labeled F_T. Three red arrows leave the bob: one straight down labeled w = mg, one continuing along the string away from the pivot labeled -mg cos theta with theta marked between it and the weight arrow, and one tangent to the arc pointing back toward equilibrium labeled -mg sin theta. Axes at the upper right define +y along the string toward the pivot and +x tangent to the arc away from equilibrium. The arrow arrangement resolves the weight into components along and across the string. The diagram identifies the tangential component as the restoring force behind the oscillation.

interactionPlan.concept: A pendulum oscillates because the tangential component of gravity, -mg sinθ, always points back toward equilibrium; for small angles this becomes approximately proportional to displacement.

interactions.label: Angle θ
interactions.teaches: Changing θ shows that the bob's arc displacement s grows with angle, while the tangential gravity component -mg sinθ changes sign and always points back toward equilibrium

interactions.label: Animate pendulum motion
interactions.teaches: During the swing, velocity reverses at the endpoints while the restoring-force arrow continually points toward the center of the motion

interactions.label: Tangential force model
interactions.teaches: The exact restoring force is nonlinear in θ, but at small angles sinθ ≈ θ, so the pendulum behaves like a simple harmonic oscillator

demo_steps.title: Displaced pendulum
demo_steps.narration: At a positive angle, gravity points straight down, but only its tangential component pulls the bob back along the arc toward equilibrium. The radial component is balanced with tension and does not restore the swing.

demo_steps.title: Drag through equilibrium
demo_steps.narration: Move θ through zero. The tangential component shrinks to zero at equilibrium, then reverses direction on the other side so it still points back toward the center.

demo_steps.title: Watch the restoring force during motion
demo_steps.narration: Start the animation and follow the red tangential-force arrow. It is largest near the endpoints, zero at the bottom, and always directed opposite the displacement.

demo_steps.title: Use the small-angle approximation
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the small-angle view. Near the vertical, -mg sinθ and -mgθ nearly match, explaining why small pendulum swings are approximately simple harmonic.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The pendulum's restoring force is not the whole weight mg, but the tangential component -mg sinθ, which becomes the linear SHM force -mgθ only for small angles.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Recreate the original layout as a clean 2D physics diagram: beige support at top, pivot near upper left, dashed vertical equilibrium line, tilted pendulum string down to the right, gray bob, and labeled force arrows starting at the bob. Use dark blue for tension F_T and red for all gravity-related arrows. The θ slider should move the bob along a circular arc of fixed radius L, rotate the string, update the pivot angle label, update the dashed arc length s, and resize/reorient the -mg sinθ and -mg cosθ arrows. In animation mode, show the bob oscillating along the same arc and optionally add a velocity arrow tangent to the path so learners can see velocity reverse at endpoints while restoring force points inward. In small-angle mode, relabel the tangential force as approximately -mgθ and visually highlight a small-angle range near the vertical, such as |θ| less than about 15 degrees.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for angle theta: the learner drags the bob along the arc, the displacement s and the -mg sin theta and -mg cos theta components update in length and direction, making clear that the tangential component is the restoring force toward equilibrium.
- Animation for pendulum motion: the learner starts the swing, the bob oscillates while the velocity and restoring-force arrows change sign through equilibrium, making clear how the force continually points back toward the center of the motion.
- Toggle between exact and small-angle views: the learner switches from -mg sin theta to the small-angle form proportional to theta, the tangential-force label and approximation range update, making clear when the pendulum behaves like simple harmonic motion.

authoredContext:
A simple pendulum is defined to have a point mass, also known as the pendulum bob, which is suspended from a string of length L with negligible mass (the figure). Here, the only forces acting on the bob are the force of gravity (i.e., the weight of the bob) and tension from the string. The mass of the string is assumed to be negligible as compared to the mass of the bob.

A simple pendulum has a small-diameter bob and a string that has a very small mass but is strong enough not to stretch appreciably. The linear displacement from equilibrium is s, the length of the arc. Also shown are the forces on the bob, which result in a net force of −mgsinθ toward the equilibrium position—that is, a restoring force.

In the figure, a horizontal bar is shown. A string of length L extends from the bar at an angle theta counterclockwise from the vertical. The vertical direction is indicated by a dashed line extending down from where the string is attached to the bar. A circular bob of mass m is attached to the lower end of the string. The arc from the mass to the vertical is indicated by another dashed line and is a length s. A red arrow showing the time T of the oscillation of the mob is shown along the string line toward the bar. A coordinate system is shown near the bob with the positive y direction aligned with the string and pointing toward the pivot point and the positive x direction pointing tangent to the arc and away from the equilibrium position. An blue arrow from the bob toward the pivot, along the string, is labeled F sub T. A red arrow from the bob pointing down is labeled w = m g. A red arrow pointing tangent to the arc and toward equilibrium, in the minus x direction, is labeled minus m g sine theta. A red arrow at an angle theta counterclockwise from w is labeled minus m g cosine theta.

Consider the torque on the pendulum. The force providing the restoring torque is the component of the weight of the pendulum bob that acts along the arc length. The torque is the length of the string L times the component of the net force that is perpendicular to the radius of the arc. The minus sign indicates the torque acts in the opposite direction of the angular displacement:

discrepancies: The generated figure adds a large gray dashed full swing-path arc and a black equilibrium dot below the pivot; the source only shows the short dashed displacement arc labeled s, not a full trajectory guide.

The tangential-force label −mg sinθ is placed close to the bob and the dashed s arc, making the central force-decomposition area more cluttered than the source where the label sits clearly to the left.
The tension label is rendered as plain text 'F_T' rather than a proper subscripted F_T, reducing fidelity to the textbook notation.
The generated diagram is slightly more diagrammatic/annotated than the source, with extra interactive explanatory affordances and optional elements not present in the static textbook figure.
evaluation.notes: The main pendulum geometry, force directions, component labels, and coordinate axes are recognizable and conceptually correct, but extra trajectory markings and some label styling/placement reduce static-source fidelity.
action_items: Remove or hide the full dashed swing-path arc and equilibrium dot in the default view so the static diagram matches the source more closely.
Reposition the −mg sinθ label farther left of the bob and away from the dashed s arc and arrows to reduce central clutter.
Render F_T with a true subscript and match the textbook math-label styling more consistently.
Keep optional small-angle and animation-specific visual additions disabled by default unless explicitly activated.

feedback.rationale: The figure is conceptually correct and highly usable, but the remaining issues are generator-level fidelity fixes such as removing extra default markings, improving label placement, and rendering subscripts properly.
